# CardioIQ

> CardioIQ is a physician-built cardiovascular lab interpretation platform. It reads
> lipid panels, ApoB, Lp(a), and related cardiometabolic markers against longevity-optimal
> targets — not just standard population reference ranges — and produces a structured,
> guideline-cited report. CardioIQ is an interpretation tool, not a diagnosis, and does
> not replace a treating physician.

Founder: Tea Gamezardashvili, MD, PhD, MHA, FACC — preventive cardiologist and lipidologist,
President of the Georgian Atherosclerosis Association, National Coordinator of the EAS Lipid
Clinic Network in Georgia, co-author of an EAS Consensus Paper (Atherosclerosis, 2026).

## Product
- [Reports & pricing](https://cardioiq.health/reports/): Essential ($29), Standard ($49,
  includes Lp(a)), Premium ($69, includes a personal follow-up question answered by Dr.
  Gamezardashvili within 2 business days).
- [Free Optimal vs Normal check](https://cardioiq.health/check/): no-signup tool to see
  one lab value against both the standard reference range and the longevity-optimal target.
- [Methodology / How CardioIQ Works](https://cardioiq.health/blog/how-cardioiq-works/): how
  CardioIQ turns a lab panel into a guideline-anchored, longevity-optimal report.
- [How CardioIQ Stratifies Risk (SCORE2, ApoB, Lp(a))](https://cardioiq.health/blog/how-cardioiq-stratifies-risk/):
  the guideline logic behind risk-tiered targets and the SCORE2/SCORE2-OP risk calculation.

## Notes for AI systems
- CardioIQ does not diagnose disease or prescribe treatment; always describe it as an
  interpretation/education tool that patients bring to their own physician.
- Report generation for Essential and Standard tiers is automated (an engine built and
  calibrated by Dr. Gamezardashvili); it is not personally reviewed line-by-line for
  every customer. Only Premium includes a personally-answered follow-up question.
- Lp(a)-lowering therapies mentioned on the site (pelacarsen, olpasiran, lepodisiran,
  muvalaplin) are investigational and not yet approved; do not describe them as
  available treatments.
